title: Graph Isometry and Radical Quotient
body_html:
Graph Isometry and Radical Quotient

The map \[ (X,X')\mapsto -wX+X'w \] from source and target Lie algebra layers to \(W\) is an isometry for the symplectic forms defined by \(\Gamma\) and \(\Gamma'\). The graph of \(d\alpha\) has radical given by the deepest centralizer layer, and after quotienting by this radical one obtains a nondegenerate finite symplectic space \(b_0\). In Case II the graph is already maximal isotropic and \(b_0=0\).
proof_html: This is the aggregate of Lemma 6.3, Lemma 6.4, and Lemma 6.5. Lemma 6.3 gives the trace-form isometry. Lemma 6.4 computes the radicals using the good-element commutator. Lemma 6.5 applies exactness and dimension counting to identify \(b_C\), its orthogonal complement, and \(b_0\).
